fantasy: Threading a gap at a speed that should not be survivable.
core_loop: Drive into the arena -> walls rush toward the craft -> steer between them -> score climbs with time and every wall cleared -> the walls speed up -> a crash ends the run -> drive again at once.
pillars: The gap is always readable before it arrives
Every crash is the player's mistake, never the camera's
Back in a run within one second of crashing

engine.rationale: Depth is part of the mechanic: a 3d arena dodger is read through a chase camera in space. Three.js with low-poly procedural geometry and vertex colours keeps the load budget close to a 2D title; textures and PBR materials are deliberately excluded.
engine.camera: Third-person chase camera, slightly high, locked behind the craft; no player camera control.

scope.progression_terminal: Progression is the personal best. The loop is deliberately open, bounded by 3 speed tiers - there is no content treadmill to feed.

session.structure: A run lasts about 60s. A session is 4 runs back to back, each starting within a second of the last ending. The first session drops straight into play with no menu; later sessions open on the title screen with the best score visible. The session ends at a natural stopping point rather than being cut off.
session.end_condition: The player sets a new personal best, or three runs pass without improvement.

retention.return_reason: I know I can hold the line through one more speed-up.
retention.progression_loop: Progression is the personal best. The loop is deliberately open, bounded by 3 speed tiers - there is no content treadmill to feed.

monetization.economy: No currency. The rewarded continue is the only economic action.

progression: Skill only: Survive 20 s in one run -> Speed tier 2 and its palette; Survive 45 s in one run -> Speed tier 3 and its palette.
difficulty: 0-15 s: Slow walls and wide gaps, so a first-time player clears walls before crashing. 15-45 s: Walls speed up 0.35 units per second each second. 45 s+: The ramp continues; only reading gaps early keeps the run alive. Assist: After three runs under 10 s, the next run's first 10 s use the opening speed.
controls: Steer left or right: Hold and drag: the craft follows the finger's horizontal position (touch). Pause: Pause button (touch).

ux.onboarding: Guided first run. Steering is one idea; the first wall shows it once.
ux.accessibility: Every audio cue has a visual counterpart, so the game plays muted - which also covers the large share of portal traffic that plays with sound off. Colour is never the only signal. Text is at least 16 CSS px at the design resolution. A reduced-motion setting (and prefers-reduced-motion) disables shake and flashes.

art_direction: Transit-signal brutalism: flat blocks of colour, oversized numerals, information first. Identity kit 'signal-brutal'. Rectangles only; 3px black borders; numerals set enormous and cropped by the viewport edge.
audio_direction: Library music loop plus short library SFX, all compressed and loaded after first play so audio never delays time to first play. Every cue has a visual twin.

assets.spec: Low-poly GLB built from a model spec: hull, canopy, two fins, engine glow; 800-3k triangles, flat-shaded

assets.spec: Low-poly GLB modules built from a model spec: floor tile with lane lines, side rail; vertex colours
assets.readability: A floor whose lines run toward the horizon so speed reads, and side rails that mark the arena's edge; both dimmer than the craft and the walls

assets.spec: Low-poly GLB built from a model spec: framed panel with emissive strips; under 1k triangles
assets.readability: A wall panel with a lit frame and emissive strips, its gap obvious from 40 units away: 'do not touch' before it arrives, in the identity's warning colour

A gradient sky that sets the horizon, darker than the walls so every wall stands out against it

assets.description: Buttons, panels and the result card, drawn in the identity kit

assets.description: Play, pause, retry, menu, sound, ad glyph

SIL Open Font License 1.1, its OFL.txt shipped beside the files. WOFF2 (TTF accepted), subset to the locales in scope (subsets: cyrillic, latin - ru, en), bundled under public/assets and loaded through the runtime asset manifest with @font-face; awaited (document.fonts.load) before the first UI frame.
